text:
- chief complaint: right knee pain and swelling after a fall while jumping on a trampoline.
- history of present illness: About four days ago, the patient slipped while jumping on a trampoline, felt a pop, and noticed rapid swelling. Ibuprofen and ice helped only slightly, and bearing weight is still difficult. Diabetes management is ongoing, though glucose checks are often missed.
- physical examination: Heart sounds normal, no murmurs or gallops; lungs clear. Right knee swelling, tenderness greater on the medial side, pain with flexion and extension, limited range of motion, negative McMurray test.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right knee pain, swelling, popping sensation at injury, pain on standing, difficulty walking.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: Meloxicam (Mobic) newly prescribed, dosage N/A. Metformin 500 mg refilled, unchanged.
- follow-up instructions: Straight-leg brace; ice knee about 15 minutes hourly; MRI of right knee; recheck hemoglobin A1c; continue metformin.
